subject: Post-call: buyer path, procurement steps & systems-in-scope
messages:
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alyssa Chen <alyssa.chen@orbitpay.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sun, 29 Nov 2026 16:12:00 -0800
Subject: Post-call recap & next steps — buyer path, procurement, systems in scope

Hi Alyssa — great to meet today, thanks for the thoughtful discussion. Quick recap and proposed next steps so nothing falls through the cracks: 

Summary from today's call:
- Primary use case: real-time risk scoring in checkout (low-latency generation + embeddings for user profiles).
- Expected q1 pilot: ~5k requests/day, peak bursts during promotions.
- Key decision criteria: latency under 200ms P95, strong data isolation controls, SOC2 + penetration test evidence.

Action items / asks from OrbitPay:
1) Please confirm the economic buyer and primary procurement contact (name + email).
2) Security intake: can you share the systems that are in-scope for your internal review (databases, S3 buckets, ETL, on-prem hosts, VPN/bastion)?
3) Attached: Redwood-Security-Questionnaire-v3.pdf (stub). Please drop answers inline or return a marked-up PDF.
4) Proposed security kickoff: 45 min with Security + Infrastructure + Procurement — suggested window: Mon 2026-11-30 or Tue 2026-12-01. What works for your team?

Internal notes for Marissa/Neha: Alyssa indicated procurement timeline ~6–8 weeks if legal redlines are standard; security will require SOC2 report and IP/network diagram. If procurement requires PO/contracting flow, we should prep a standard SOW + pricing cadence.

Next steps (my plan):
- Wait for Alyssa's confirmation on buyer + systems-in-scope.
- Send calendar invite for kickoff once OrbitPay confirms attendees.
- Prep our security POC package: SOC2 summary, questionnaire answers, sample isolation architecture, and the network diagram template.

Thanks — I’ll follow up as soon as I hear back.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Account Executive — Redwood Inference
kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com
(415) 555-0184

Attachment: Redwood-Security-Questionnaire-v3.pdf (stub)
Related link: https://hubspot.com/deal/ORB-2026-1379

From: Alyssa Chen <alyssa.chen@orbitpay.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Tom Redding <tom.redding@orbitpay.com>, Security Team <secops@orbitpay.com>
Date: Sun, 29 Nov 2026 19:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-call recap & next steps — buyer path, procurement, systems in scope

Kimberly — thanks for the clear recap and the questionnaire. Quick answers inline:

Economic buyer: Tom Redding (CTO) — tom.redding@orbitpay.com
Procurement contact: procure@orbitpay.com (cc'd on internal threads; formal PO comes from Teresa in procurement)
Security reviewers: SecOps (secops@orbitpay.com) + AppSec (appsec@orbitpay.com)

Systems in scope (initial):
- Public-facing API cluster (k8s) — production
- User profile DB (Postgres, managed) — contains PII (hashed identifiers)
- Payments DB (Oracle) — limited access, contains transaction metadata
- S3 buckets (us-west-2) — model artifacts + logs
- Internal ETL service (on-prem) that pulls batches from the payments DB

Security asks: SOC2 Type II report, recent pen test summary, and a high-level network diagram. I uploaded the current diagram to Drive (link below).

Kickoff availability: I can do Mon 2026-11-30 09:00–10:00 PT or Tue 2026-12-01 11:00–12:00 PT. Prefer 09:00 on Monday so Tom can join before his afternoon meetings.

I'll start filling out the questionnaire and will return it by EOD Monday.

—Alyssa
Alyssa Chen
Head of Integrations, OrbitPay
alyssa.chen@orbitpay.com
(617) 555-2233

Drive link: https://drive.google.com/drive/fake-network-diagram

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 06:45:00 -0800
Subject: RE: Post-call recap & next steps — buyer path, procurement, systems in scope

Kim — looping in a couple internal items we should prepare before the kickoff: 

1) Legal: I will surface standard SLA language and a minimal data processing appendix (DPA) for OrbitPay's review. Ask: can we get any non-negotiable clauses they expect? Procurement often flags highly customized indemnities.
2) Security pack: Neha, can you pull the latest SOC2 summary + pen test high level and draft an architecture note that maps our typical private deployment (VPC peering + restricted egress) to the OrbitPay systems listed?
3) Technical: request that Alyssa confirms whether the ETL service has a DMZ or requires a VPN peering arrangement — this affects whether on-prem connectors are in-scope for our managed agent or need an air-gapped workflow.

Procurement timeline note: expect 6–8 weeks for enterprise customers if legal needs standard redlines. If they need custom clauses it could push to ~10 weeks. We should propose a light pilot SOW (30 days) that can be scoped independent of full enterprise contracting.

I can join the kickoff at 09:00 PT on Mon.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Solutions Lead, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com

> On Nov 29, 2026, at 7:03 PM, Alyssa Chen <alyssa.chen@orbitpay.com> wrote:
> > Kimberly — thanks for the clear recap and the questionnaire. Quick answers inline:...

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alyssa Chen <alyssa.chen@orbitpay.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>, Tom Redding <tom.redding@orbitpay.com>, procure@orbitpay.com
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 07:18:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-call recap & next steps — buyer path, procurement, systems in scope

Thanks Alyssa — that is super helpful. Confirming the Monday 09:00 PT kickoff and proposed attendees: Tom (CTO), SecOps/AppSec, Procurement, Kimberly (AE), Marissa (Solutions), Neha (Security). I'll send a calendar invite to the group now.

Prep pack I will attach to the invite (for review before the meeting):
- Redwood-Security-Questionnaire-v3.pdf (stub) — please return with inline answers if possible
- SOC2 summary + pen test high-level (Neha will attach)
- Lightweight pilot SOW + pricing sheet (sales doc)
- OrbitPay network diagram (you uploaded) — we will review scopes against that diagram

A few clarifying Qs before the kickoff so we can prep the right engineers:
- Does the on-prem ETL service initiate outbound connections to cloud (pull) or do you expect an inbound connection requirement?
- Are S3 buckets under a shared account that hosts other teams' data, or are they dedicated to payments and risk?

If you can answer those two now, we can tailor the architecture note.

Thanks — invite sent.

Best,
Kimberly

Attachment (invite prep): orbitpay-network-diagram-v2.png (stub)
Related link: https://hubspot.com/deal/ORB-2026-1379

From: Alyssa Chen <alyssa.chen@orbitpay.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Tom Redding <tom.redding@orbitpay.com>, procure@orbitpay.com, Security Team <secops@orbitpay.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 10:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-call recap & next steps — buyer path, procurement, systems in scope

Kimberly / team — confirming Monday 09:00 PT works for us and Tom will attend. Quick answers to your clarifying questions: 
- ETL behavior: on-prem ETL initiates outbound pulls to our cloud staging endpoint (secure TLS) — no inbound firewall openings required.
- S3 ownership: buckets are dedicated to risk services (separate AWS account, us-west-2).

We will return the questionnaire completed by EOD Monday and upload the pen test summary to the Drive link. Procurement (procure@orbitpay.com) will follow up on the PO template if the pilot SOW looks good.

See you Monday.

—Alyssa

Drive link (updated): https://drive.google.com/drive/fake-network-diagram
